comparison: baseline (Phase 6, frozen backbone) vs fine-tuned (Phase 7, partial unfreeze + focal loss)

finetune_attempt_1.config: 30 unfrozen layers, dropout 0.3, focal loss, lr 1e-5
finetune_attempt_1.pattern: val_auc declined every epoch after epoch 1 (0.698 -> 0.695 -> 0.691 -> 0.688) - classic overfitting signature

finetune_attempt_2.config: 15 unfrozen layers, dropout 0.5, focal loss, lr 1e-5
finetune_attempt_2.pattern: same shape as attempt 1: peak at epoch 1, steady decline after (0.696 -> 0.693 -> 0.691 -> 0.691)

honest_conclusion: Fine-tuning did NOT meaningfully improve over the frozen-backbone baseline in either configuration tested (0.696-0.698 vs baseline's 0.697 - differences are within noise).

Both fine-tuning configs show the identical pattern: best result at epoch 1, immediate decline afterward - halving trainable parameters (645K -> 338K) and raising dropout (0.3 -> 0.5) did not change this pattern, suggesting the limitation is not primarily about model capacity/overfitting from too many parameters.

Most likely explanation: ~7,035 training images is not enough data for DenseNet121's upper layers to genuinely adapt to chest X-ray characteristics beyond what the frozen ImageNet features already capture, at least at this learning rate and layer-unfreezing depth.

Decision: proceeding to Phase 8 evaluation with BOTH checkpoints (baseline_best.keras and finetuned_best.keras) for a full per-class comparison, rather than continuing to tune hyperparameters against this same small validation set (1,500 images), which risks overfitting the validation set itself through repeated manual adjustment.

This is a legitimate, reportable finding - not a failure. Possible future directions (not pursued here due to time/data constraints): more training data (pull additional NIH archives), unfreezing fewer/different layers, or a lower fine-tuning learning rate.
